sources.title: Breloc cu minifigurină aurie, product 850807
sources.summary: The manufacturer describes a decorative accessory fixed to a ring and chain that can attach to keys or a backpack. These optional uses support the key/backpack accessory sense. This exemplar does not make every breloc metallic, a watch ornament or a branded object.
sources.licence: No open reuse licence verified; original factual summary only.

sources.title: Breloc, product 3220202
sources.kind: First-party description from an independent company
sources.summary: An ordinary accessory is described for keys, a bag or a backpack, with a wrist strap. This independently supports real Romanian key/bag use; no price, stock, licensed character or universal material claim is retained.
sources.licence: No open reuse licence verified; original factual summary only.

sources.title: BOPI Designs and Models 4/2002, inscribed breloc design
sources.publisher: OSIM and original filed design description
sources.access: Web reader rejected 15,935,442-byte PDF; original downloaded directly into own task scratch and locally read
sources.locator: Printed page 577, actual PDF page 54/index 53 in 166-page original
sources.summary: A physical inscribed breloc design has several shapes with an attachment opening and a key motif. This verifies written use before 2010. Technical registration does not measure audience recognition or establish modern key/backpack use on its own.
sources.licence: No open reuse licence verified. No descriptions/drawings copied into the repository.
sources.locator_correction: An initial local page-range command confused printed 577 with PDF page 577. Corrected to actual index 53 before making a verified source claim.

sources.title: BOPI trademark applications, 6 March 2024
sources.kind: Original official application/classification text, not a dictionary
sources.summary: The list distinguishes key accessories, leather/nonmetallic forms, watch-shaped items and jewelry forms. It refutes a universal metal claim and cautions against collapsing key accessory and jewelry senses. Classification does not establish synonyms or broad recognition.
sources.licence: No open reuse licence verified; original factual summary only.

sources.title: BOPI Inventions 3/2006, attachable bottle-shaped recipient
sources.locator: Printed page 23/PDF index 24, application a200500813A0, lines 1112–1127
sources.summary: The abstract describes a threaded closure fitting a recipient opening; one variant closes both the opening and a tube. This verifies physical container-closure usage before 2010. It establishes neither cork material, wine dependence, a cooking recipe nor equivalence to every lid.
sources.licence: No open reuse licence verified; original factual summary only.

sources.title: Rubber bottle stopper, product 10682546
sources.kind: First-party seller product/material record; description authorship not independently established
sources.summary: The product record specifies rubber and bottle closure use. This concrete example refutes an all-cork definition. Seller description is not a universal lexical definition or conservation guarantee.
sources.licence: No open reuse licence verified; original factual summary only.

sources.title: LILLVIKEN sink plug, product 70311541
sources.summary: A sink plug retains water with its matching siphon. Components include plastics, steel, synthetic rubber and brass. This supports a drain-plug application distinct from the initial bottle-stopper scope. Compatibility is model-limited; neither all-model fit nor universal material follows.
sources.licence: No open reuse licence verified; original factual summary only.

sources.title: Bathtub waste system with plug, product PRO_102139
sources.locator: Title and application fields, lines 13 and 53–57
sources.summary: The catalogue names a bathtub waste system with a plug and specifies bath applications with a 52 mm opening. This corroborates the drain-plug hypothesis. It does not prove every bathtub has that construction or that a bottle stopper fits a bath.
sources.licence: Copyright 2026 Geberit shown; no open licence verified.

sources.title: Collection campaign for plastic bottle closures
sources.kind: Original Romanian reporting used for lexical recognition context
sources.locator: Date and participant interview, lines 35 and 72–77
sources.summary: The report uses ordinary vocabulary for plastic closures removed from bottles in a collection campaign. It supports familiar bottle usage; campaign quantities, personal medical information and policy assertions are not proposed graph facts.
sources.licence: No open reuse licence verified; original factual summary only.

recognition.limit: Promising everyday vocabulary with real written use across time/companies, not a measured cross-generational audience result or an independent A1/A2 approval.
